title: A Oath for the Crown
premise: Emrys Fairweather keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in stolen memories, bottled names, and other impossible things—until he finds tonight's date inscribed in a century-old prophecy, naming him as either the king's unmaker or his savior. Hunted by the guild he serves and haunted by memories that may not be his own, Emrys discovers the king has been hollowed out and replaced by a crown-fed parasite called the Regent, which survives by consuming royal memory. To free the king, Emrys must surrender the one memory anchoring his own identity—the truth of who he was before the guild took him in. In the end, Emrys unbinds the king at the cost of forgetting himself entirely; the restored monarch, remembering everything, gives Emrys a new memory of gratitude and belonging, and the thief begins again—not invisible this time, but chosen.
about_author: Isandro Underhill is the pen name of a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three collections of books that technically did not exist. They write fantasy from a cluttered desk overlooking a harbor, fueled by strong tea and stronger opinions about prophecy.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. On an ordinary night, Emrys audits the Vellum Guild's ledgers—entries for stolen first kisses, bottled grief, a river's childhood—and steals a small memory for himself to feel alive. The beat is quiet competence masking loneliness, establishing his gift: he can lift and hold memories like coins.

chapters.title: Ink That Was Already Dry
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Cross-checking an old acquisition, Emrys finds a prophecy ledger written a century ago bearing tonight's exact date and his own description: 'the keeper of accounts shall open the crown.' He tells no one. The emotional beat is dread curdling into denial—he built his life on being unwritten.

chapters.title: The Guild Takes Notice
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Guildmistress Sarelle summons him; someone has read the prophecy page before he could hide it. She offers protection in exchange for the ledger, but her kindness feels like a snare. Beat: paranoia—Emrys realizes invisibility was always an illusion the guild permitted.

chapters.title: A Memory Not Mine
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Among his private hoard, Emrys finds a memory he cannot place: snow, a woman's voice calling a name that isn't Fairweather. It predates his earliest recollection. Beat: vertigo—if his hoard holds foreign memories, what else in his head was installed?

chapters.title: The Palace Thieves
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The guild contracts Emrys to steal from the royal vault—a job no one refuses. Inside, he witnesses the king speaking to empty air in a voice not his own. Beat: awe tipping into horror as Emrys glimpses the thing behind the king's eyes.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Researching in forbidden archives, Emrys learns of the Regent: a parasite of accumulated royal memory that devours each monarch from within, wearing them until nothing remains. The current king has weeks left. Beat: grim purpose replaces fear—this is why the prophecy named him.

chapters.title: Sarelle's Price
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Sarelle reveals she knows what Emrys is planning and forbids it: the Regent is the guild's oldest client, trading stability for memories. Defy her and every thief in the city hunts him. Beat: betrayal—his protector was a warden all along.

chapters.title: The Name in the Snow
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Following the foreign memory's details, Emrys finds a village and an old woman who recognizes his face: he is the son of a court memory-keeper, smuggled out as a child when the last king began to fail. Beat: grief and relief entwined—his identity has a source after all.

chapters.title: Blood Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. His mother's line kept the rite of unbinding, sealed in a memory only a blood heir can safely open. Opening it nearly unmakes him; he wakes knowing the rite but having lost a day of his life to pay for it. Beat: sacrifice foreshadowed—every answer costs a piece of himself.

chapters.title: Hunted by the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Guild assassins corner him; he survives by stealing the lead hunter's courage mid-fight, leaving the man weeping. But Sarelle now holds proof of his bloodline. Beat: desperate flight—he is no longer a keeper of accounts but an entry in someone else's.

chapters.title: An Ally Behind Bars
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys seeks Wren, a disgraced palace chronicler imprisoned for writing true histories. Wren confirms the Regent's cycle and reveals the prophecy has two endings—one where Emrys frees the king, one where he becomes its next vessel. Beat: resolve sharpened by terror.

chapters.title: The Hollow King
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Smuggled into the king's presence by Wren's old contacts, Emrys meets Aldric: a gentle, fading man who remembers his daughter's face but not her name. Beat: tenderness—the mission stops being abstract; the king is a person being eaten alive.

chapters.title: Princess Ilsette
chapters.summary: POV Ilsette. The king's daughter catches Emrys fleeing her father's chambers. Instead of raising alarm, she demands the truth—and offers help, having watched her father disappear for years. Beat: unexpected alliance; two people who love a hollowed man.

chapters.title: The Regent Speaks
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The Regent, aware of him now, appears in dreams wearing Emrys's own forgotten face, offering restoration of every stolen memory in exchange for walking away. Beat: temptation—it knows exactly what he most wants because it helped take it.

chapters.title: Ledgers Burned
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Sarelle burns the prophecy and declares Emrys dead to the guild, unleashing its full network. Ilsette's safehouse falls; Wren is taken. Beat: darkest hour—everything Emrys built to stay hidden is ash, and his friends pay for it.

chapters.title: The Rite of Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. In the crypt beneath the palace, Emrys and Ilsette prepare the rite: it requires a keeper to hold the Regent's attention with their own deepest memory while the blood-heir speaks the unbinding words. Beat: solemn preparation—Emrys decides which memory to offer without telling anyone.

chapters.title: Coronation of Ash
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The Regent moves early, forcing the rite mid-ceremony before the assembled court. Emrys steps into the light, opens his hoard, and lets the creature pour into him. Beat: climax begins—sacrifice made public, identity offered as bait.

chapters.title: Inside the Crown
chapters.summary: POV Emrys (interior). Within the Regent, Emrys walks centuries of consumed kings, finding young Aldric's original self still screaming behind the walls. He feeds the Regent his anchor memory—the truth of his name and mother—until the creature, glutted, loses grip on the king. Beat: white-hot climax of loss.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV Ilsette. With Emrys vacant-eyed and the Regent distracted, Ilsette speaks the blood-rite. The Regent tears free of both men and, with nothing left to wear, unravels into dust. Aldric collapses whole; Emrys does not wake. Beat: victory shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: A Blank Page
chapters.summary: POV Ilsette. Emrys wakes with no past: no guild, no mother, no name he trusts. The healed king sits with him daily, returning pieces through testimony. Beat: tender aftermath—identity revealed as something others can help rebuild.

chapters.title: Given Memory
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. King Aldric performs the one rite left to a restored monarch: gifting a memory freely given. He gives Emrys the memory of this rescue—of being chosen, fought for, and loved by strangers who became family. Beat: grace answering sacrifice.

chapters.title: A New Entry
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Months later, Emrys opens a new ledger in the rebuilt guild under Ilsette's reformist hand: memories returned, never taken. He writes the first entry in his own hand—his own name, newly chosen. Beat: resolution—invisibility traded for authorship of self.
